setlist.title: It Must Have Been the Roses

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dancin' in the Street** (3 reviews): Reviewer points to the grooves in this performance as a highlight; Hot jam; around nine minutes everyone can be heard, and Jerry plays slide [3][7][13]
- **Estimated Prophet** (2 reviews): Video shows Bob bearded, a Travis Bean guitar and Moog keyboard; Jerry visibly enjoys his solo; Reviewer likes its sound and first-set placement, calling it ever-improving, with a cool tone from Jerry [5][6]
- **Big River** (1 review): Energetic first-set performance, with praise for Keith's playing [6]

## The recordings

- **gd77-04-26.aud.goodbear.260.sbefail.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 18 songs; 147 min; rated 3.07/5 by 15 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls it a poor audience tape, nearly unbearable, and possibly the only recording of the show; Says sound is very good for an audience tape, with occasional audience chatter; Sound is middling, best heard on headphones [2][3][7][8][10][13]

## Around the show

- Video shows Donna restrained while Mickey, Bill, Keith and Phil seek a little more prominence [5]
- Fourth night of the tour; band seemed to conserve energy, though the venue was nice and the first set laid back [6]
- Reviewer attended at age 15, travelling from Queens by train and bus, and was stranded overnight in Passaic after missing the last bus [9]
- Sound quality is reported as comparable to the 4/25 recording from the same source [1]
- Advises getting the nights before and after this show first, as the performance is unremarkable [2]
- Mississippi Half-Step is strong but not quite up to later 1977 versions [7]
- The 4/27 show has a better setlist and much better audio than this one [8]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd77-04-26.aud.goodbear.260.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by Teddy Goodbear; source: Audience Recording [1]. Also: Same source as the partial DVD/VCD video that circulated earlier; A partial DVD/video of the show circulates, with the same video quality as the 4/27 video [3][8]
